messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Pagerduty triggered: high-memory OOMs on runtime-pool-3 (gpu-node-group) - page sent to #incidents - priority: P1
Jamie (oncall): I’m on it. spinning up the incident thread. anyone seeing customer-facing errors?
Sasha: getting a handful of 503s from the hosted API, mostly long-context completions. CS just flagged 3 customers complaining about latency/timeouts.
Leon: attaching quick snapshot from metrics:
```
gpu_node: gpu-12
mem_total_gb: 48
mem_used_gb: 46.9
fragmentation_pct: 79
kv_cache_pages: 1.2M
last_gc: 2026-03-15T02:12:03Z
batch_size_p50: 8
batch_size_p95: 32
```
Dana: thanks. hypothesis: KV cache fragmentation + large tail batch requests causing page faults and GPU OOM on allocation. seen similar pattern when batch size spikes + long kv prefix.
Mike SRE: confirming logs - runtime shows repeated `cudaMalloc` failures and immediate retries, then a cascade where memory pressure climbs and we fail larger allocations. sample log: `E tensorflow: cudaMalloc failed: out of memory at 0x7f...`
Jamie (oncall): mitigation proposals: 1) temporarily lower max_batch_tokens and max_batch_concurrency for the pool, 2) enable KV cache eviction for >16k prefix sessions, 3) route degraded traffic to fallback small-model (latency up but avoids OOM). which can we flip fastest?
Leon: I can push a conservative config change to reduce `max_batch_tokens` from 2048 -> 512 and `max_concurrency_per_gpu` from 64 -> 24. That should reduce peak allocation pressure. takes ~30s to apply and affects all workers in the pool.
Sasha: CS: prefer targeted approach if possible - route only high-latency customers to fallback rather than global batch limits. can we do per-tenant routing quickly?
Dana: we have a routing rule ready as config: `route.policy=latency_based && tenant in [custA,custB] -> fallback_model=small-v2`. I can deploy that in ~4 mins. still want global batch limits to avoid node crash.
incident-bot: action created: ACTION-1123 reduce_batch_tokens on runtime-pool-3 assigned to Leon (due 2056789035)
Jamie (oncall): Leon please apply the batch change, Dana please prepare the per-tenant routing. Mike, collect logs/traces and start timeline. Sasha, coordinate CS messaging.
Leon: applying change now. CLI:
```
redwoodctl runtime update --pool runtime-pool-3 --set max_batch_tokens=512 --set max_concurrency=24
```
Leon: change applied. nodes rolling config. watching mem.
Mike SRE: sharing timeline entries:
- 02:01:12Z first cudaMalloc FAIL on gpu-12
- 02:02:45Z retry spikes, fragmentation jumps from 52% -> 79%
- 02:05:30Z node enters OOM kill path, pods restart
- 02:07:03Z majority of failed requests are long-context (>10k tokens) completions
- 02:09:10Z batch limit change propagated
- 02:10:22Z observed drop in immediate allocation failures

Jamie (oncall): Leon, any improvement on memory stats now?
Leon: memory used settling. new snapshot:
```
mem_total_gb: 48
mem_used_gb: 41.1
fragmentation_pct: 61
kv_cache_pages: 1.1M
```
still high but we’re out of the immediate OOM loop.
Sasha: CS: started an outbound to affected customers: basic info + we are mitigating, ETA 30m. asked for logs from customer A to correlate.
Dana: deploying per-tenant routing now to push custA/custB to small-v2 fallback. command: `redwoodctl route apply --policy file://fallback-custA.json` - applied.
incident-bot: note: fallback routing active for tenants [custA, custB] (applied 2056789080)
Mike SRE: collecting KV cache stats by tenant. interesting: 90% of the large allocations come from 12 sessions across 3 tenants with persistent huge prefixes. suggests hot long-lived sessions are the root cause.
Jamie (oncall): good signal. next steps: short term: keep reduced batch limits + per-tenant fallback for 1 hour and monitor. medium term: implement automatic kv eviction thresholds and a soft limit on prefix length with graceful warnings.
Leon: adding a temporary evict policy on pool: `kv_cache.evict_threshold=0.75` - applied to runtime-pool-3. will free pages gradually.
Mike SRE: logs show `kv_cache.evict` triggered, recovered ~800MB on each node over 3 cycles.
Sasha: CS: customers updated, many appreciate the quick fallback. one customer still seeing errors; asking for trace id.
Jamie (oncall): Sasha share the trace id and I'll check whether their requests hit the fallback or were throttled.
Sasha: trace id TID-2056789099 attached.
Mike SRE: TID-2056789099 shows request landed at 02:04:59Z, allocation failed, retried 3x then ultimately 503. It pre-dates our batch change. customer likely hit the tail before mitigation.
Dana: recommendation for post-incident: 1) permanent eviction policy by prefix-age and size, 2) guardrail on max_batch_tokens per tenant, 3) add a runtime detector to auto-lower batch sizing when fragmentation > 70%.
Leon: operational playbook note: add an oncall runbook step to check `kv_cache.stats` and `fragmentation_pct` and flip `max_batch_tokens` if fragmentation > 70. also create a safe rollback plan: if we see latency spike > 2x after lowering batch tokens, revert and route to fallback model instead.
Jamie (oncall): documenting timeline and lessons in the incident doc. tagging Postmortem owner: Dana.
incident-bot: incident state: mitigated -> monitoring. severity: P1 -> P2 for now.
CS-bot: customer-impact summary: 3 customers affected with intermittent 503s and increased latency between 02:01Z - 02:09Z. SLA impact logged.
Sasha: will keep customers updated, planning a follow-up once postmortem available.
Jamie (oncall): final checks: keep watch on mem and fragmentation for 30m. if stable, we can gradually relax batch limits tomorrow with a canary. thanks all. :thumbsup:
